title: Sheaf scalar-Hom evaluation chain map and input naturality
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe, $\varphi:R\to S$ a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings, $E=S\otimes_R-$ the sheafification of sectionwise scalar extension and $U$ restriction of scalars, both applied termwise to unbounded cochain complexes [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Write $T(A)=S\otimes_R A$ for the underlying $R$-linear sheaf tensor, termwise. Write $H_R(P,J)=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,J)$ and $H_S(K,N)=\mathcal Hom_S^\bullet(K,N)$ for the actual product Hom complexes [def-pur-hom-complex]; their local degree-$n$ sections have coordinates $f^i:P^i|_W\to J^{i+n}|_W$ on $\mathcal C/W$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. All pure tensors below mean their images under the tensor sheafification units [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], and evaluation means the actual product projection followed by evaluation at the identity object of the slice.
For arbitrary $R$-complexes $P,J$, $S$-complex $N$, and $S$-linear chain map $q:EJ\to N$, there are an $R$-linear chain map
$$\alpha_{P,J}:T H_R(P,J)\longrightarrow H_R(P,TJ)$$
and a unique $S$-linear chain map
$$\sigma_{P,J,q}:E H_R(P,J)\longrightarrow H_S(EP,N)$$
with the following formulas over every slice, in every degree $n$ and coordinate $i$:
$$\alpha(s\otimes f)^i(p)=s\otimes f^i(p),\qquad \sigma_q(s\otimes f)^i(t\otimes p)=st\,q^{i+n}(1\otimes f^i(p)).$$
Both commute with slice restriction and the signed Hom differentials. For chain maps $u:P'\to P$, $v:J\to J'$, $w:N\to N'$ and $q':EJ'\to N'$ with $q'\circ Ev=w\circ q$, their input naturality equations are
$$H_R(u,Tv)\circ\alpha_{P,J}=\alpha_{P',J'}\circ T H_R(u,v),$$
$$H_S(Eu,w)\circ\sigma_{P,J,q}=\sigma_{P',J',q'}\circ E H_R(u,v).$$
The notation $H(u,v)$ means precomposition with $u$ and postcomposition with $v$ in each coordinate. No flatness, boundedness, projectivity or K-injectivity is assumed; neither comparison is asserted to be invertible.

proof.text: Fix $n,W$, $s\in S(W)$ and $f\in H_R^n(P,J)(W)$. For each $i$ define a map on $\mathcal C/W$ by sending a section $p\in P^i(V)$, for $a:V\to W$, to the tensor-unit image $s|_V\otimes f^i_V(p)\in (TJ^{i+n})(V)$. This is $R(V)$-linear in $p$: for $r\in R(V)$, $s|_V\otimes f^i_V(rp)=s|_V\otimes r f^i_V(p)=r(s|_V\otimes f^i_V(p))$. It commutes with restriction since both $f^i$ and the tensor units do. These maps form a section $a_W(s,f)$ of $H_R^n(P,TJ)$. Addition in $s,f$ is preserved; for $r\in R(W)$ both $a_W(\varphi(r)s,f)$ and $a_W(s,rf)$ have coordinate $s|_V\otimes r|_V f^i_V(p)$. Thus $(s,f)\mapsto a_W(s,f)$ is $R(W)$-bilinear. Its restriction along $W'\to W$ is $a_{W'}(s|_{W'},f|_{W'})$, as checked on every further object of the slice.

proof.text: The module tensor universal property extends $a_W$ uniquely to an $R(W)$-linear map $S(W)\otimes_{R(W)}H_R^n(P,J)(W)\to H_R^n(P,TJ)(W)$. The restriction identity in step 1, together with uniqueness on pure tensors, makes these maps a morphism of presheaves of $R$-modules. The target is a sheaf by the product Hom construction. The module sheafification universal property therefore gives $\alpha^n:T H_R^n(P,J)\to H_R^n(P,TJ)$. Its formula is the one in the statement. Throughout the proof, equality of maps out of a sheafified tensor will be tested by precomposing the sheafification unit on every object, and then on pure tensors, using these same two universal properties. Equality into a product Hom sheaf means equality of every coordinate as a map on every slice object.

proof.text:
Check the chain equation for $\alpha$ by the equality test of step 2. For a degree-$n$ family $f$ and $p\in P^i(V)$, the degree-$(n+1)$ coordinate of $d\alpha(s\otimes f)$ is
$$s|_V\otimes d_J^{i+n}f^i(p)-(-1)^n s|_V\otimes f^{i+1}(d_P^i p)=s|_V\otimes (d_H f)^i(p).$$
Here $d_{TJ}=1\otimes d_J$ and the signed Hom differential is precisely that of the cited definition. The last expression is $\alpha(s\otimes d_H f)^i(p)$. Tensor bilinearity and uniqueness through sheafification extend the equality to the source sheaf. Thus the degree maps $\alpha^n$ form the required $R$-linear chain map.

proof.text: Let $\eta_J:J\to UEJ$ have degree components $x\mapsto 1\otimes x$, using the scalar-extension sheafification units. These are $R$-linear because $1\otimes rx=\varphi(r)\otimes x$, compatible with restriction, and satisfy $d_{EJ}(1\otimes x)=1\otimes d_Jx$. Hence $\eta_J$ is a chain map. Put $h=(Uq)\eta_J:J\to UN$. Functoriality of the product Hom complex gives the $R$-linear chain map $b=H_R(1_P,h):H_R(P,J)\to H_R(P,UN)$ with $b(f)^i(p)=q^{i+n}(1\otimes f^i(p))$.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-slice-scalar-hom-chain-adjunction] with the actual $R$-complex $P$ and $S$-complex $N$. Its chain isomorphism $\theta_{P,N}:U H_S(EP,N)\to H_R(P,UN)$ has inverse sending a local family $k^i$ to the $S$-linear maps $t\otimes p\mapsto t k^i(p)$. Compose the chain map $b$ from step 4 with this inverse to obtain $\beta:H_R(P,J)\to U H_S(EP,N)$. It is $R$-linear, a chain map, and compatible with slice restriction. Its coordinates are
$$\beta(f)^i(t\otimes p)=t\,q^{i+n}(1\otimes f^i(p)).$$
The cited statement explicitly supplies the inverse on all slices, its compatibility with restriction, and its chain property for unbounded product Hom complexes, without flatness. This step uses no scalar-evaluation comparison as an input.

source.place: Tags 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), 03CZ (lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict), 03EK (section-tensor-product); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes). Agent coordinate construction from these universal properties.

proof.text: Write $G=H_S(EP,N)$. On each object $W$ the rule $(s,f)\mapsto s\beta_W(f)\in G^n(W)$ is $R(W)$-bilinear: $\beta$ is $R$-linear and the $R$-action on $UG$ is through $\varphi$. Extend it by the module tensor universal property to $S(W)\otimes_{R(W)}H_R^n(P,J)(W)\to G^n(W)$. This extension is $S(W)$-linear since for $a\in S(W)$ both images of $a(s\otimes f)$ and $a\,s\beta_W(f)$ are $as\beta_W(f)$, and tensors generate the module. Restriction compatibility follows from that of $\beta$ and of scalar multiplication. We have a morphism of presheaves of $S$-modules, so the $S$-module sheafification universal property gives $\sigma^n:E H_R^n(P,J)\to G^n$. Step 5 yields exactly $\sigma^n(s\otimes f)^i(t\otimes p)=st\,q^{i+n}(1\otimes f^i(p))$ on every slice.

source.place: Tags 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), 03CZ (lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict), 03EK (section-tensor-product); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes). Agent coordinate construction from these universal properties.

proof.text:
The signed differential of $G$ is $S$-linear. Since $\beta$ is a chain map, on every outer pure tensor
$$d_G\sigma^n(s\otimes f)=s\,d_G\beta(f)=s\beta(d_Hf)=\sigma^{n+1}(s\otimes d_Hf).$$
Explicitly, its coordinate at $t\otimes p$ is
$$st\bigl(d_N^{i+n}q^{i+n}(1\otimes f^i(p))-(-1)^n q^{i+n+1}(1\otimes f^{i+1}(d_P^ip))\bigr)
=st\,q^{i+n+1}(1\otimes(d_Hf)^i(p)),$$
using $d_Nq=q d_{EJ}$ and $d_{EJ}(1\otimes x)=1\otimes d_Jx$. The inverse formula in the cited slice adjunction determines each inner map from its values at $1\otimes p$, so this coordinate check is an equality of sheaf maps on the slice. The tensor and sheafification equality test of step 2 now proves the outer chain equation. Thus $\sigma$ is an $S$-linear chain map.

proof.text: Suppose $\widetilde\sigma$ is another $S$-linear chain map with the asserted formula. On each object and outer generator $s\otimes f$, the families $\widetilde\sigma(s\otimes f)$ and $\sigma(s\otimes f)$ agree after evaluation at $1\otimes p$, in every coordinate and over every further slice object. The injectivity of the slice adjunction $g\mapsto(p\mapsto g(1\otimes p))$ makes their coordinate maps equal; the product Hom definition then makes the families equal. The module tensor and sheafification universal properties give $\widetilde\sigma^n=\sigma^n$ for every $n$, hence equality of chain maps. This proves the stated uniqueness without supposing tensor sheaf sections globally have pure-tensor representatives.

source.place: Tags 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), 03CZ (lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict), 03EK (section-tensor-product); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes). Agent coordinate construction from these universal properties.

proof.text: For the first naturality equation, work in degree $n$ on $s\otimes f$, coordinate $i$, over an arbitrary further slice object $V$, at $p'\in P'^i(V)$. Its left side evaluates to $s|_V\otimes v^{i+n}(f^i(u^i(p')))$. Its right side evaluates to the identical expression, since $H_R(u,v)(f)^i=v^{i+n}f^iu^i$. Coordinate equality on all $V$, followed by the outer tensor and sheafification equality test, proves $H_R(u,Tv)\alpha_{P,J}=\alpha_{P',J'}T H_R(u,v)$. The maps being compared are chain maps since $u,v$ are chain maps and $H_R$ is the bifunctor of the cited definition.

source.place: Tags 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), 03CZ (lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict), 03EK (section-tensor-product); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes). Agent coordinate construction from these universal properties.

proof.text:
For the second equation use the same outer tensor and evaluate the inner coordinate on $t\otimes p'$. The left side is
$$st\,w^{i+n}q^{i+n}(1\otimes f^i(u^i(p'))),$$
because $Eu(t\otimes p')=t\otimes u(p')$ and $w$ is $S$-linear. The right side is
$$st\,q'^{i+n}(1\otimes v^{i+n}(f^i(u^i(p')))).$$
These agree by the assumed equality $q'Ev=wq$ in degree $i+n$, applied to $1\otimes f^i(u^i(p'))$. The slice adjunction detects equality of the inner $S$-linear maps, product coordinates detect equality of Hom sections, and tensor generation followed by sheafification uniqueness detects equality of the outer maps. This proves $H_S(Eu,w)\sigma_{P,J,q}=\sigma_{P',J',q'}E H_R(u,v)$. All constructions used arbitrary local families and termwise scalar extension, so no bound or finiteness condition entered.
